chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Rabi' al-Asamm, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda' and Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Abu al-Ward, both of them from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man divorces his wife with a single divorce while in his illness, and then remains in that illness until her waiting period expires, she inherits him provided she has not married another. If she has married after the expiration of the waiting period, then she does not inherit him.

key_terms.مَرَضِهِ: his illness (specifically the illness in which he dies)

ai.seo_question: Does a wife inherit her husband if he divorces her while ill and dies from that illness?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the specific ruling of 'inheritance of the sick' (mirath al-marid) within the context of a single revocable divorce, emphasizing that the wife retains her inheritance rights provided she remains unmarried throughout the iddah period. It highlights the Shia scholarly distinction that the illness must be the cause of death for this specific rule to apply, linking the marital bond's continuity during iddah directly to the transfer of wealth upon death.
